newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Nusamba says withdrawing from Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Nusamba says withdrawing from Busang.

text.p: Indonesia's Nusamba Group, linked to President Suharto, said on Monday it was withdrawing from the scandal-hit Busang gold project.

It said the decision to pull out of the project, in which it had a 25 percent stake, followed surveys of Busang by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc and Canadian consulting firm Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd.

"As a result of FCX's due diligence efforts, which have now been confirmed by the Strathcona audit report, Nusamba will notify Bre-X that it is withdrawing from the Busang project," Nusamba said in a faxed statement.

The Nusamba Group, chaired by business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, is 80 percent owned by three charities headed by President Suharto, and 10 percent each by Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd released a report from Strathcona in Canada on Sunday night in which Strathcona said assays of test cores from the key area of Busang had shown no commercial gold content.
The Strathcona report also referred to falsification of assay values at Busang on an unprecedented scale.
Nusamba said it had received a copy of the report.
Bre-X had earlier estimated gold reserves at Busang in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province at over 70 million ounces.
But Bre-X stunned the mining world last month when it said the amount of gold might have been over-estimated.

After a bitter battle with another mining giant over control of Busang, the small Canadian mining company had reached agreement in February to keep 45 percent of the property, with 40 percent going to Indonesian interests and 15 percent to Freeport, which was to develop the mine.
Freeport and the Indonesian partners had said their participation depended on a thorough "due diligence" survey of the property.
